Which of the following items could be considered constraints when performing a network design?(Choose all that apply.)
Timeline, staffing, organizational politics, and budget can all constrain a WLAN project. They influence what can be designed and delivered.
As a device starts to shift to lower PHY rates, what factors usually influence a device decision to shift to lower PHY rates?(Choose all that apply.)
PHY rate adaptation responds to link quality. Signal degradation, packet loss, interference, and retransmissions are all indicators that a lower rate may be more reliable.

A business traveler from North America is in Europe. The hotel only provides coverage in 2.4 GHz. The traveler connects to the hotel's SSID and notices an AP in the hotel room. However, the laptop reports a very low RSSI when connected. The traveler does not have the same problem when connecting in the lobby. What would be the most likely cause of the low RSSI in the hotel room?
The AP in the room is transmitting on channel 13 and the traveler associated to a non-channel 13 AP located elsewhere.
The AP in the room is using Bluetooth instead of Wi-Fi.
The AP in the room is using ZigBee instead of Wi-Fi.
The switchport that the AP is connected to is only capable of transmitting at 10 Mbps.
Channel 13 is permitted in many European regulatory domains but is not available to some North American client configurations. Region settings can therefore prevent discovery.
During lunch time in the break room of a company, Wi-Fi connectivity on the 2.4 GHz band is intermittent. Every other time of the day, it works fine. What's the likely cause of this issue?
Employees are using their cell data instead of using the Wi-Fi
The AP in the cafeteria keeps rebooting due to lack of PoE budget on the switch
Microwaves in the cafeteria are interfering with the Wi-Fi on the 2.4 GHz band
Toasters and ovens are heating up the air, raising the noise floor with the Wi-Fi on the 2.4 Ghz band
Microwave ovens can emit energy in the 2.4 GHz band while operating, raising interference and causing intermittent Wi-Fi performance nearby.

Use a plastic cover that could blend in with the environment
Lock the AP inside of a metal box
Place the APs in between walls and I-beams
Use an 802.11b AP, so it looks old enough to be in a museum
A purpose-designed nonmetallic cover can improve appearance while avoiding the severe RF attenuation caused by metal enclosures; manufacturer guidance and warranty terms still apply.
An MSA commonly addresses at least which two legal categories?
A nondisclosure agreement establishes a confidentiality obligation and limits how the customer's proprietary information may be shared.
For what purpose is SSID hiding generally useful?(Choose all that apply.)
Preventing guests from attempting to join the secured corporate network
Obscuring the network name from potential attackers
Minimizing help desk calls from users and guests attempting to join the wrong network
Preventing legitimate corporate users from finding the guest network

Hiding an SSID can reduce casual discovery and accidental connection attempts, but it is not a security control because the SSID can still be learned from management frames. The supplied answer key also cites reduced help-desk calls.
SSID hiding is not generally recommended because some frames require inclusion of the SSID. In what frames is the SSID always included?
Association Request frames include the SSID so the client can identify the network it is attempting to join. Hidden SSIDs therefore remain discoverable.
What is the minimum PoE budget needed on a switch to support 6 (six) APs that can only be powered using IEEE 802.3at if no other details are provided?
Six APs at the IEEE 802.3at maximum PSE allocation of 30 W each require 180 W of PoE budget.
When viewing channel utilization information from a protocol analyzer, if high channel utilization is occurring, what should you ensure does not exist?
A high percentage of low PHY rates
An RF signal generator causing an RF DoS
Low PHY rates consume more airtime per frame. A high proportion of slow transmissions can drive channel utilization upward even when payload throughput is modest.

A cable with 2.5 dB of loss is used to measure the return loss of an antenn a. The measured value in-band is shown to be larger than 20 dB. What is the actual return loss of the antenna, and is it considered to be a reasonable value?
A return-loss value greater than 15 dB indicates relatively little reflected power. The measurement must account for the test cable's known loss so the antenna result is interpreted correctly.

Jitter is a measurement of the variance of the number of frames received from an application for a specific time interval.
Jitter is a measurement of average latency based on a sample of >100 frames.
Latency is a measurement of the time delay experienced in the delivery of a frame.
Latency is a measurement of the time required to transmit two subsequent frames.
Jitter and latency are two important metrics for measuring the quality and performance of wireless
For what purposes are VPNs typically used in modern WLANs?(Choose all that apply.)
Remote AP tunneling to a corporate WLAN controller or VPN concentrator
Client device connectivity to corporate resources from unsecured public networks
Initial 802.11 authentication with the AP and subsequent data encryption
Tunneling APs and WLAN controllers to cloud-based management platforms
Tunneling APs and WLAN controllers to RADIUS and token servers
Bridging client connectivity in ad hoc networks
VPNs can securely tunnel traffic from remote APs back to a corporate controller or concentrator, and can provide client devices with encrypted access to corporate resources from untrusted networks.
What differences exist between VLANs in wireless and wired domains?
Wireless VLANs are not effective for segmenting the available services and network permissions available to clients. Wired VLANs are effective for this purpose.
Wireless VLANs are never carried in 802.11 frames that cross the wireless medium. VLAN identifiers are always carried in Ethernet frames to indicate the proper VLAN.
Wireless VLANs do not always segment traffic into separate broadcast domains on the wireless medium. Wired VLANs do segment broadcast domains on the wired network.
Wireless VLANs are not an effective way to utilize a single set of infrastructure equipment to provide different services to different client groups. Wired VLANs are effective for this purpose.
A wireless VLAN assignment does not necessarily create a separate over-the-air broadcast domain for every client group. Wired VLANs do segment Layer 2 broadcast domains on the Ethernet network.
An enterprise customer is subject to the highest standards for network uptime. When designing their wireless network, you should consider which of the following?(Choose all that apply)
The failover of the wireless network only
The failover of the wired network only
The failover of the wireless and wired network
The physical aspects such as power and cabling

High availability depends on both logical failover (wireless and wired network paths/services) and physical resilience (power, cabling, switches, and uplinks). A WLAN is only as available as its dependencies.
